newsitem.title: CANADA: PanCanadian posts record earnings for '96.
newsitem.headline: PanCanadian posts record earnings for '96.

text.p: PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd, Canada's largest publicly traded upstream energy company, on Thursday reported record earnings and cash flow for 1996, even though its natural gas production dropped.

PanCanadian, the petroleum arm of conglomerate Canadian Pacific Ltd, said it earned C$346 million, or C$2.75 per share, up from C$228 million or C$1.82 per share in 1995. The increase came despite an after-tax writedown on international operations of C$58 million.
Cash flow jumped to C$1 billion or C$7.87 per share from C$805 million or C$6.42 per share last year.
The company said it was a big benefactor of strong prices for both oil and natural gas.

"When production increases lagged earlier this year, our employees increased their efforts to bring us back on track to attaining our targets," PanCanadian president David Tuer said in a statement. "There is no question that we have been helped by price this year, but it is with the drill bit that we continue to add value to this company."
The company said gas production averaged 694 million cubic feet per day in the fourth quarter, down from 778 MMCFD in 1995.
It said the drop was because of a 40 MMCFD adjustment for a swap of gas properties for oil properties which was effective in June. By the end of 1996, the firm was producing 740 MMCFD, it said.
It said crude oil production for the year averaged 132,723 barrels per day, up from 117,441 in 1995.
PanCanadian said its outlook for 1997 was very positive, although it continued its conservative view of world oil prices.
"We expect the benchmark price for crude oil to decline from current levels and natural gas prices to strengthen slightly above the average price of C$1.60 in 1996," the company said.
"Our C$1 billion 1997 capital program will be balanced between crude oil and natural gas with continued focus on the Western Canada Sedimentary Basin." ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
